articles.title: Unmanned Underwater Vehicles Market Projected to Reach US$ 46.62 Billion by 2035 | Astute Analytica
articles.summary: The global unmanned underwater vehicles (UUV) market, valued at US$5.49 billion in 2025, is projected to surge significantly, reaching US$46.62 billion. This robust growth underscores increasing demand for advanced underwater capabilities in defence for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, alongside applications in scientific research and commercial exploration. Aspiring officers should recognize UUVs as a vital component of modern naval strategy and technological advancement.

articles.title: AI and the Next Economy
articles.summary: AI labs are promoting a compelling narrative regarding Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). They foresee AGI unlocking astonishing productivity and significantly boosting GDP. This story is particularly attractive to those building or investing in these new technologies, highlighting AI's profound potential to reshape global economies and drive innovation.

articles.title: Review – Absolute Green Lantern #10: Gold and Blood
articles.summary: The latest Green Lantern #10 comic explores a significant shift in its narrative arc. While initial stories focused on cosmic threats, the new storyline delves into the implications of the Lanterns becoming public knowledge. This development introduces fresh challenges and explores the impact of their powers and presence within a broader, public context, evolving beyond purely extraterrestrial dangers.

articles.title: Russia sends submarine to escort tanker the US tried to seize off Venezuela: Report
articles.summary: Russia has deployed a submarine and other naval vessels to escort an empty, ageing oil tanker attempting to evade a US blockade near Venezuela. This move, reported by the Wall Street Journal, underscores heightened geopolitical tensions and Russia's assertive support for Venezuela against US sanctions. It highlights the projection of naval power and potential for international flashpoints over resource control and sovereignty disputes.

articles.title: There are no signs of more Russian and Chinese ships near Greenland
articles.summary: Chinese and Russian naval presence in Greenlandic waters is raising significant U.S. security concerns. These ships are perceived as a growing threat to American interests, especially considering the strategic importance of the Arctic region. The U.S. criticizes Denmark for its apparent inaction, highlighting potential vulnerabilities in regional defence and international maritime security.
